description: Build McCreight's radix priority search tree and answer bounded three-sided point-reporting queries.

source.title: Priority Search Trees
source.author: Edward M. McCreight
source.algorithm_attribution: Section 2 radix priority search tree: fixed x-interval bisection, y-min heap ordering, and three-sided enumeration.
source.implementation_status: bounded clean-room static-build/query profile; algorithm description only

input.point_constraints: x values and labels are individually unique; points are inserted in input order.
input.query_semantics: Report labels for all points with x0 <= x <= x1 and y <= y1; x intervals are closed.

output.meaning: Each query's 8-bit label-hit mask is packed into the corresponding result byte, in query order; bit label is set when that labeled point is reported.
output.encoding: OR over query_index of (hit_mask << (8*query_index)); Q is at most 7, so the scalar is nonnegative and lossless for every query mask.

contract.data_structure: McCreight's Section 2 radix priority search tree on fixed x interval [0,32); each distinct-x point appears once, x intervals bisect, and parent y is <= each child y.
contract.insertion: Process points in input order. A strictly smaller y displaces the current node point; ties do not swap. Insert the displaced point into the child selected by its x against the interval midpoint.
contract.query: Depth-first enumeration prunes a subtree when its x interval misses [x0,x1] or its y-minimum exceeds y1. Report the node label if its point satisfies both bounds.
contract.primary_method: Build the priority search tree by the source's radix insertion rule, then query through interval overlap and the y-min heap invariant.
contract.independent_method: Scan each query against every original point and form its label mask directly.

workspace.meaning: Eight point nodes with x intervals and heap/split links, seven query records, a bounded traversal stack, and packed result state.
